guitar.evidence: Tracy Chapman is a singer-guitarist known for acoustic-driven folk songs like 'Fast Car'; commonly associated with Gibson/Guild-style acoustics in performance, though not a singularly iconic specific model.

tone.target: clean Strat neck pickup with light breakup and springy room
tone.profile: clean Strat neck pickup with light breakup and springy room
tone.summary: A classic country/blues tone achieved using a light boost for attack, followed by a clean Fender-style amp model (US Deluxe) into a 2x12 cabinet, finished with minimal compression and spring reverb.

rig.name: Tracy Chapman - Give Me One Reason - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Provide slight grit and enhance attack without heavy overdrive.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used to simulate the light breakup/grit required, as dedicated low-gain preamps are not available.

blocks.purpose: Bypass (No distortion needed for clean tone).
Simulate the bright, clean Fender-style amp tone.
Provide the required bright, compact sound profile (Fender-style).
Smooth dynamics and enhance the 'twang' of the neck pickup.
Bypass (No wah needed for this style).
Keep the tone dry and focused on phrasing.
blocks.gap: Delay is optional but kept minimal to avoid muddying the clean sound.

blocks.purpose: Provide the required short, springy room ambiance.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the default 2x12 IR for a more vintage, open-air sound that complements the clean Fender tone.

proposals.reason: Enhance vintage character and open-air feel.
